title: Comprehensive AmiExpress, AmiX and MAXs corpus reanalysis
methodology: Computed SHA-256 from every uploaded byte stream.
Parsed every ZIP member and every LHA header.
Re-read source and documentation even for byte-identical redistributions.
Classified source languages and scanned symbols, structures, functions and numeric command usage.
Separated host implementation evidence, public SDK evidence, wrapper evidence and behavioral corpus evidence.
Did not promote command-number coincidences across API families to semantic equivalence.

reviewed_finding.finding: Source corpus of practical AmiExpress doors, primarily Amiga E, including BBSLink, global wall/last-callers and Discord announcements. It demonstrates contemporary door behavior, networking and use of host-facing calls, but mixes door clients with external web backends.

reviewed_finding.finding: Complete AmiExpress host source in Amiga E. It exposes the implementation context behind AEDoor-facing behavior, node/session state, command dispatch, transfer, HTTP/FTP and configuration subsystems. It is host implementation evidence, not by itself a stable public door API contract.
DoorStatus is a concrete MAXs door and confirms runtime use of the message protocol and status/session interactions.
Volume 5 reanalysed from payloads; primarily implementation/deployment evidence.

Volume 1 of a large compiled/documented MAXs door collection; valuable for breadth and deployment conventions but weaker than source for API semantics.

Reanalysis confirms a documented C wrapper SDK with headers, libraries, demos and callable operations. It is a portability layer over host behavior and should remain distinct from the underlying host-native protocols.
Launcher and scripts for raw programs; no new source-level door contract.
